stages.caption: Preserve natural movement while preparing active support.
stages.question: Who needs this assistance?
stages.notes: This work concerns an active artificial knee for older adults who need knee replacement and also experience sarcopenia. We begin with the person, follow the biomechanical implant into its nonlinear spring, and then ask how reinforcement learning could control assistance. The motion on the cover is a visual reference, not evidence of an assistance benefit. 한국어: 기존 ICCAS 제목만 유지하고 현재 진행 중인 연구로 구성한다. 표지 보행 연출은 대상 노인에 대한 보조 성능 결과가 아니다. title: Background
lead: Aging affects the joint and the muscles that move it.
source: Pioneer_2022_proposal.pdf: PDF p11/printed p2 and PDF p40/printed p31 · Mizner et al.,2005 · MyoAssist open-source models

stages.caption: Joint degeneration can limit everyday movement in older adults.
stages.notes: The Pioneer proposal begins with older adults who need knee replacement because of joint degeneration. Keep the same person visible while approaching the knee. The joint-degeneration comparison is an explanatory illustration, and the generic musculoskeletal model is not an elderly patient-specific reconstruction. Introduce the muscles after explaining what replacement changes. 한국어: 수술을 고려하는 고령층과 관절 손상에서 출발한다. 근감소증은 다음 단계에서 노화의 맥락으로 자연스럽게 연결한다.
stages.subtitle: Joint degeneration can limit everyday movement
stages.body:
Joint degeneration can limit everyday movement.

The target is an older adult needing knee replacement.
stages.takeaway: Aging affects both joints and muscles.

stages.caption: Replacement changes the joint surfaces. Muscles still produce movement.
stages.question: What happens when muscle strength also declines?
stages.notes: Conventional total knee replacement changes damaged joint surfaces using metal components and a polyethylene insert. The surrounding muscles remain responsible for producing movement. Retain the same knee, its neighbouring bones and the muscle context while inserting the conventional components. First inspect the polyethylene insert in top view. Restore the oblique view before separating and preparing the bones. Insert the femoral component upward and the tibial component downward, then reduce the joint. These are educational display movements and resection, not a validated patient fit. 한국어: 일반 인공관절의 표면 치환 역할을 보여주고, 여전히 움직임을 만드는 근육으로 시선을 이어간다.
stages.subtitle: Joint surfaces change; muscles still drive movement
stages.body:
Replace the joint surfaces.

The muscles still produce movement.

stages.caption: Quadriceps strength can drop sharply during early recovery after knee replacement.
stages.question: How could we support weakened muscles?
stages.notes: Mizner et al. studied 20 patients with unilateral knee osteoarthritis, tested on average 10 days before and 27 days after primary total knee arthroplasty. Quadriceps strength decreased by 62% compared with the preoperative value. The audience graph normalizes preoperative strength to 100 and reconstructs the reported postoperative level as 38; these are relative values, not measured torque units, prevalence or fabricated individual data. No error bars are invented. This is a small 2005 study of early postoperative weakness, not a sarcopenia prevalence, long-term deficit, inevitable outcome for every patient or evidence that our device solves it. The Pioneer target still includes older adults with sarcopenia, but postoperative activation failure and muscle atrophy must not be conflated with the sarcopenia diagnosis. Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15866968/ ; https://doi.org/10.2106/JBJS.D.01992. 한국어: 수술 전 약 10일과 수술 후 평균 27일에 측정한 20명 연구에서 대퇴사두근력이 수술 전보다 62% 감소했다. 수술 전=100, 수술 후=38로 정규화하여 표시한다. 62%는 환자 비율이나 장기적 근감소증 수치가 아니며 초기 수술 후 근력 저하이다. 우리 장치의 보조 효과를 보여주는 결과도 아니다.
stages.subtitle: Muscle strength can fall sharply in early recovery
stages.body:
Joint replacement does not immediately restore strength.

Early recovery can involve substantial muscle weakness.

stages.caption: Assistance can be worn outside the body.
stages.notes: Show three actual open-source MyoAssist human–device models: HMEDI_L1 (hip assistance via cables), OpenExo_L1 (ankle assistance via a strut), and DephyExoBoot_L1 (ankle assistance via a boot). Preserve the source devices, their body attachments and the source human geometry. Canonical standing and source-keyframe motion are kinematic presentation replays, not trained assistance policies or evidence of a walking benefit. The examples illustrate external assistance and attachment locations; their appearance is not evidence of discomfort, clinical effectiveness or comparative superiority. 한국어: MyoAssist에서 실제 사람 모델에 장착된 HMEDI L1, OpenExo L1, Dephy ExoBoot L1을 보여준다. 기본 기립 자세와 원본 키프레임으로 구성한 기구학 재생이며 학습된 보조 보행이나 보조 효과 검증 결과가 아니다. 몸에 고정하여 힘을 전달하는 구조를 설명하고 외골격 전반의 불편함·열등성으로 확대하지 않는다.
stages.subtitle: Assistance can be worn outside the body
stages.body:
Wearable devices can support movement.

They transmit support through attachments to the body.

stages.caption: Could the implant also provide active support?
stages.question: What mechanism could make this possible?
stages.notes: Return to exactly the conventional knee-replacement components shown in the surgery step, then bring in the original BLDC motor model beside them. The composition introduces the idea of combining joint replacement and active assistance. Do not reveal the completed Pioneer assembly in this step or imply that the motor attaches directly to the conventional implant as shown. The arrangement is a research concept rather than a surgically or mechanically validated assembly. Carry the motor-to-joint idea into the Hardware chapter, where the actual mechanism and transmission are explained. 한국어: 2단계의 일반 인공관절에 기존 BLDC 모터를 더하는 개념으로 표현한다. 우리 완성품은 아직 공개하지 않고, 그 결합을 실제로 구현하려면 어떤 기구가 필요한지 다음 Hardware 장으로 이어간다.
stages.subtitle: Could the implant also provide active support?
stages.body:
Combine joint replacement with a compact motor.

A research concept for active assistance.

title: Hardware
ko: 무릎의 움직임을 보존하고 구동 기능 더하기
lead: Follow the same implant from its joint mechanism to its motor and gears.
source: Moon, thesis interim presentation, 2024-12-10: slides3–15 · original AAKJ CAD/URDF and restored kinematics · native-knee primary references

stages.caption: The biomechanical joint was the starting point before active assistance.
stages.question: Why is a simple hinge insufficient?
stages.notes: The previous team analyzed knee motion and developed the equivalent four-bar foundation before my contribution. Natural movement involves more than rotation about one stationary hinge. Reference the interim presentation printed page 4 (PPTX slide 6, image22.gif) and the sagittal bone-motion GIF on printed page 3 (PPTX slide 5, image17.gif). Recreate their flexion, roll/glide and medial-side pivot vocabulary in Three.js using actual native bone surfaces. The source kinematic pivot is used only as the explanatory replay timing; this is not recovered cadaveric motion. Compare a qualitative native-knee illustration with the source implant. The source bones are real meshes, while comparison rollback and pivot are authored explanatory motion, not measurements from the hinge-only STS trace. 한국어: 선행 팀의 기여를 명시한다.
stages.subtitle: Natural knee motion combines rolling and gliding
stages.body:
The knee rolls and glides as it bends.

Its motion is more than a fixed hinge.
stages.takeaway: The knee is more than a hinge.

stages.caption: An equivalent four-bar lets the joint centre move during flexion.
stages.question: How does that movement create medial rotation?
stages.notes: Track a frame rigidly fixed to the J2–J3 femoral link, with its neutral origin at URDF [0,0,0.021] m. Its trajectory is reference-point dependent; do not call J2 itself the femoral frame. The exact orthographic sagittal view shows the projected path. Follow the four equivalent centres. J1 is the Peek_Bushing cam-follower centre; J2 is the curved-slot circle centre in Condyle_Right, an equivalent point rather than a physical pin. J3 is R3 and J4 is R2. The source cam constraint is represented by an equivalent connection without inventing another physical bar. 한국어: J2 등가점을 실물 핀으로 설명하지 않는다.
stages.subtitle: A four-bar reproduces the moving reference
stages.body:
An equivalent four-bar recreates femoral motion.

The aim is to mimic knee motion.
stages.takeaway: Recreate the motion with a linkage.

stages.caption: One bend couples Joint 3 descent, slider retreat and medial rotation.
stages.question: How does the same motion look from above?
stages.notes: Keep the source side view while following Joint 3 displacement into the guide and slider. The constrained path provides the connection between flexion and the axial motion examined next. Genuine source components and restored kinematics are retained. 한국어: 측면에서 J3 변위와 실제 슬라이더 구속을 먼저 이해시킨다.
stages.subtitle: Flexion drives slider translation
stages.body: One bend couples Joint 3 descent, slider retreat, and medial-pivot rotation.

stages.caption: The same bend produces rotation around the medial side.
stages.question: Where does active torque enter?
stages.notes: Now turn to the axial view of the same mechanism. Follow the constrained slider motion into medial-pivot rotation. This is restored source kinematics, compared with authored qualitative native motion rather than a patient-specific measured match. The actual Slider_Cover mesh remains traceable. 한국어: 같은 기구를 축방향에서 보며 굴곡과 내측회전의 연동을 설명한다.
stages.subtitle: Slider motion produces medial-pivot rotation
stages.body:
The same motion rotates about the medial side.

Flexion and axial rotation are mechanically coupled.

stages.caption: The motor and gears add a drive path to the biomechanical mechanism.
stages.question: What if the person moves the joint first?
stages.notes: Reveal the motor and follow the gears toward the elastic element and output. Compact reduction provides useful torque but makes reverse interaction important. The person can initiate movement too, so we must examine the same path from the output back toward the motor. 한국어: 모터·기어 전달과 사람 주도 역방향 상호작용을 같은 단계에서 연결한다.
stages.subtitle: Motor torque passes through the gears
stages.body:
Motor → gears → joint

Add active drive while keeping the coupled knee motion.
stages.takeaway: Add power through the same mechanism.

stages.caption: Motor, series spring and output form one drive path.
stages.question: Why should that element be nonlinear?
stages.notes: Explode the original motor assembly, the two source spring leaves and the output hub without reparenting any source joint. The motor shaft remains owned by the motor assembly; the splined bevel gear is the output-side visual anchor. Presentation-only offsets are removed on exit. Stay in the same implant as the view approaches the original spring location. Series elasticity can separate rigid motor drive from compliant interaction at the output. The next chapter defines the SEA and explains the stiffness trade-off and actual spiral design. Native-knee background references: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15330038/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11132285/. 한국어: 같은 인공관절 내부의 원본 스프링 위치로 접근하며 다음 SEA 설명을 준비한다.
stages.subtitle: A spring couples the drive to the output
stages.body:
A series spring connects the drive to the output.

Compliance is part of the drive design.
stages.takeaway: Put compliance in the torque path.

title: Nonlinear Torsion Spring
lead: A spring in the torque path links mechanical compliance to assistance control.
source: Moon, thesis interim presentation, 2024-12-10: slides3–15 · original spring CAD · separate archived representative FEA

stages.caption: A series elastic actuator places a spring between the motor drive and the load.
stages.question: What should this spring allow?
stages.notes: SEA means series elastic actuator. The spring lies in the torque-transmission path between the motor-side drive and the output. Relative rotation deforms the spring and generates elastic torque. This gives the person a compliant interaction instead of an ideally rigid transmission. 한국어: 처음 듣는 청중을 위해 SEA의 위치와 역할을 먼저 정의한다.
stages.subtitle: Elasticity in the torque path
stages.body:
SEA means series elastic actuator.

The spring lies in the torque path.

stages.caption: Low stiffness permits yielding, but useful torque can require more deflection.
stages.question: Can one constant stiffness serve both needs?
stages.notes: With a linear spring, low stiffness needs more relative deflection for the same torque, while high stiffness resists motion more strongly. This is a design trade-off rather than proof that every conventional SEA fails. We want yielding behavior at small loading and stronger torque transfer as deformation grows. 한국어: 낮은 강성과 큰 토크 전달 사이의 설계 상충을 설명한다.
stages.subtitle: Low and high stiffness: a design trade-off
stages.body:
Low stiffness: compliant interaction, but more travel.

High stiffness: torque with less travel, but less compliance.
stages.takeaway: One fixed stiffness is a compromise.

stages.caption: The design seeks a stiffness that rises as the spring winds.
stages.question: How can geometry change that stiffness?
stages.notes: A nonlinear torque–deflection relationship is the mechanical objective. It changes how much added torque follows an added relative angle. This explains why a nonlinear spring is useful before showing the specific spiral geometry. No performance curve on this conceptual step is an experimental or learned result. 한국어: 목표 곡선의 개념과 검증된 특성곡선을 구분한다.
stages.subtitle: Compliant first, stiffer as winding grows
stages.body:
Let stiffness rise with winding.

Balance yielding with torque transmission.

stages.caption: Contact shifts equivalent stiffness from the lower spring to the upper spring.
stages.question: What makes the lower spring stiffen?
stages.notes: Before turn contact, k1 << k2, so keq approximately follows k1. Once turn contact raises k1 well above k2, keq approximately follows k2 instead. The labels refer to tangent stiffness; k1 is the initially compliant lower unit and k2 is the upper unit. These are conceptual limits, not a fitted source-CAD law. In an ideal quasistatic serial pair, both springs transmit the same torque and their deflections add. The compliant unit deforms more initially; the stiffer unit also deforms, rather than waiting with zero torque. The axial source-CAD view exposes strip width and coil spacing; axial depth is a separate dimension. 한국어: 직렬 연결은 같은 토크이며 변위가 합쳐진다는 점을 분명히 한다.
stages.subtitle: Contact shifts the stiffness-setting spring
stages.body:
The lower spring initially takes most of the deflection.

Contact limits its extra motion; further deflection shifts to the upper spring.
stages.takeaway: Contact shifts which spring sets the stiffness.

stages.caption: Neighboring-turn contact increases tangent stiffness.
stages.question: How can the design be examined through analysis?
stages.notes: Identify strip width a, axial depth b and coil gap as separate dimensions. The native spring does not acquire nonlinearity from an invented variable-width profile. The historical concept uses turn approach and the winding limit to change additional compliance, with more added deflection then shared by the stiffer serial unit. This design illustration is not solved contact or a calibrated native spring law. Axial depth cannot be inferred from a top view alone. 한국어: 폭a·축방향 깊이b·코일 간격을 구분하고 실제 원본에 없는 가변 폭 형상을 주장하지 않는다. 다음 해석은 별도 대표형상이다.
stages.subtitle: Contact produces a steeper torque response
stages.body:
As the gap closes, neighboring turns engage.

Less free flexure produces higher tangent stiffness.

subtitle: Why the Series Elastic Element Is Nonlinear
notes:
Stage 0: SEA means series elastic actuator. The spring lies in the torque-transmission path between the motor-side drive and the output. Relative rotation deforms the spring and generates elastic torque. This gives the person a compliant interaction instead of an ideally rigid transmission. 한국어: 처음 듣는 청중을 위해 SEA의 위치와 역할을 먼저 정의한다.

Stage 1: With a linear spring, low stiffness needs more relative deflection for the same torque, while high stiffness resists motion more strongly. This is a design trade-off rather than proof that every conventional SEA fails. We want yielding behavior at small loading and stronger torque transfer as deformation grows. 한국어: 낮은 강성과 큰 토크 전달 사이의 설계 상충을 설명한다.

Stage 2: A nonlinear torque–deflection relationship is the mechanical objective. It changes how much added torque follows an added relative angle. This explains why a nonlinear spring is useful before showing the specific spiral geometry. No performance curve on this conceptual step is an experimental or learned result. 한국어: 목표 곡선의 개념과 검증된 특성곡선을 구분한다.

Stage 3: Before turn contact, k1 << k2, so keq approximately follows k1. Once turn contact raises k1 well above k2, keq approximately follows k2 instead. The labels refer to tangent stiffness; k1 is the initially compliant lower unit and k2 is the upper unit. These are conceptual limits, not a fitted source-CAD law. In an ideal quasistatic serial pair, both springs transmit the same torque and their deflections add. The compliant unit deforms more initially; the stiffer unit also deforms, rather than waiting with zero torque. The axial source-CAD view exposes strip width and coil spacing; axial depth is a separate dimension. 한국어: 직렬 연결은 같은 토크이며 변위가 합쳐진다는 점을 분명히 한다.

Stage 4: Identify strip width a, axial depth b and coil gap as separate dimensions. The native spring does not acquire nonlinearity from an invented variable-width profile. The historical concept uses turn approach and the winding limit to change additional compliance, with more added deflection then shared by the stiffer serial unit. This design illustration is not solved contact or a calibrated native spring law. Axial depth cannot be inferred from a top view alone. 한국어: 폭a·축방향 깊이b·코일 간격을 구분하고 실제 원본에 없는 가변 폭 형상을 주장하지 않는다. 다음 해석은 별도 대표형상이다.

Displacements are shown at true scale. Source: assets/motion/spring-analysis-report.md ; assets/motion/spring-analysis-summary.json. 한국어: 실제 원본 스프링 시각화와 별도 대표 해석 형상을 명확히 분리한다.

stages.caption: Why a Teacher and a Student?

title: Conclusion
lead: A biomechanical implant, nonlinear spring and limited-sensing control form one research path.
source: Current design and preliminary simulation status · docs/control-evidence.md

stages.caption: Preserve joint motion, shape compliance and prepare support.
stages.question: What must be verified before useful assistance is established?
stages.notes: Return to the same human–implant scene and connect the four contributions without introducing a new performance claim: the biomechanical mechanism preserves coupled knee motion; the motor adds an active path; nonlinear series elasticity shapes interaction; the observer and imitation student provide a limited-sensing execution route. The present result is nominal sit-to-stand execution in a coupled simulation. It is not evidence of an elderly patient benefit, a learning advantage or completed physical validation. 한국어: 하드웨어→비선형 스프링→제어의 이유를 하나로 회수한다. 학생 구현을 계획 단계라고 되돌리지 않는다. The next work is to close the coupling and contact audits, calibrate the spring and device-side sensing, test varied initial conditions and disturbances, and compare valid matched tasks before claiming useful assistance. Continuous walking additionally needs anticipatory spring-state control within motor limits. The limited-sensing student already exists; its benefit, robustness and transfer remain to be established. 한국어: 구현된 학생과 남아 있는 검증을 구분한다. 과제 대상인 고령층·근감소증 조건으로 이어지는 검증이 다음 단계다.
